topic: What if a sugar cube of neutron star landed on your table
hook: What happens if a sugar cube of neutron star lands on your kitchen table?
on_screen_hook: A sugar cube weighing a *billion* tons

blocks.narration: What happens if a sugar cube of neutron star lands on your kitchen table? It weighs about a billion tons.
blocks.visual: A glowing cube of star matter punching through a kitchen table

shots.visual: A sugar-cube-sized cube of glowing blue-white star matter one inch above a wooden kitchen table, crackling with light, the wood already splintering under it
beats: the cube drops the last inch onto the wood
the tabletop splinters outward in a ring
the cube sinks straight into the table

shots.visual: Dana in a sunny home kitchen holding a coffee mug, staring at a smoking hole punched through the middle of her wooden kitchen table
beats: Dana flinches back from the table
her coffee mug slips from her hand
the mug shatters on the floor

shots.visual: A bathroom scale on white kitchen floor tiles with a tiny glowing blue-white cube resting on it

blocks.narration: That's about as heavy as a mountain. No table, no floor, not even solid rock could slow it down.
blocks.visual: The cube outweighs a mountain and bores down through a house

shots.visual: A giant brass balance scale on a grassy plain: a whole snowy mountain sits on one pan, a tiny glowing cube on the other
beats: the mountain's pan sinks
the cube's pan slams down level with it
the beam settles, perfectly balanced

shots.visual: Cross-section of a two-story suburban house and the rock layers under it, a glowing blue-white dot at the kitchen floor
beats: the glowing dot punches through the kitchen floor
it rips through the basement slab
it drills down through the rock, leaving a glowing trail

blocks.narration: Now flip it. Drop a sugar cube onto a neutron star from waist height. It hits at over three million miles an hour.
blocks.visual: A sugar cube dropped onto a neutron star

shots.visual: A robotic arm's metal claw holding an ordinary white sugar cube above the glowing, perfectly smooth surface of a neutron star, black space behind
beats: the claw snaps open
the sugar cube drops away from it
it shrinks toward the glowing surface

shots.visual: The impact point on a glowing blue-white neutron star surface, a streak of white light plunging toward it
beats: the streak of light hits the surface
a blinding white flash bursts outward
a shockwave ring races across the surface

blocks.narration: Except it never lands as a cube. The gravity is so extreme it stretches the sugar into a thread.
blocks.visual: The sugar cube stretched into a thread by gravity

shots.visual: An ordinary white sugar cube falling through black space above a glowing blue-white neutron star
beats: the cube stretches taller
its bottom corners pull downward
it thins out like taffy

shots.visual: White sugar crystals pulling apart into one long glittering thread, lit blue from below
beats: the crystals pull apart
they stretch into one long glittering thread
the thread snaps tight and races downward

blocks.narration: A star heavier than our Sun, squeezed twelve miles wide. Now picture one sugar cube of it, on your kitchen table.
blocks.visual: A neutron star over a city, then back to the kitchen table

shots.visual: A glowing blue-white neutron star hovering low over a city skyline at dusk, about as wide as the city
beats: the star spins fast
twin beams of light sweep across the sky
the city lights flicker below

shots.visual: Dana leaning over her wooden kitchen table, wide-eyed, a tiny glowing blue-white cube hovering just above the wood
beats: the cube glows brighter
Dana leans in closer
the cube starts to drop toward the wood

cta: Follow for one impossible what-if a day.

captions.hook_line: A sugar cube of neutron star would weigh about a billion tons on Earth 🤯
captions.body: NASA: one sugar cube of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth, about as much as a mountain. The star packs more mass than the Sun into a ball about 12 miles across, and anything dropped 1 meter onto it hits at around 1,400 km/s, stretched into a stream on the way down.
captions.comment_prompt: What should we drop on a neutron star next?

youtube_title: What If a Sugar Cube of Neutron Star Hit Your Table?

sources.claim: Sugar cube of neutron star material weighs about 1 billion tons, about as much as a mountain; about 20 km (12.5 miles) across, mass of a sun
Object falling 1 m on a 12 km neutron star reaches about 1,400 km/s (over 3 million mph); tidal forces stretch it apart before impact; typical mass ~1.4 suns

visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, dramatic light, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field

cast.Dana: a woman in her mid-30s, curly red hair tied in a bun, olive-green apron over a white T-shirt, round tortoiseshell glasses
